<Canvas>
<Panel x={200} y={160} w={620}>
<Heading>Pythagorean theorem</Heading>
<Text>In a right triangle, the two shorter sides squared add to the longest side squared.</Text>
<Math highlight>a^2 + b^2 = c^2</Math>
<Text tone="muted">a and b are the legs; c is the hypotenuse, opposite the right angle.</Text>
</Panel>
<Panel x={900} y={160} w={560}>
<Heading>Squares on each side</Heading>
<List>
<Item>a-square: area a^2</Item>
<Item>b-square: area b^2</Item>
<Item>c-square: area c^2</Item>
</List>
<Note kind="tip">The two small squares together fill exactly the big one.</Note>
</Panel>
<Panel x={200} y={620} w={620}>
<Heading>Check a 3-4-5 triangle</Heading>
<Equations>3^2 + 4^2 &= 9 + 16 \\ &= 25 \\ c &= \sqrt{25} = 5</Equations>
<Note kind="check">The right angle makes c the longest side.</Note>
</Panel>
<Plot fn="sqrt(25 - x^2)" xmin={-5} xmax={5} points="3,4" label="a=3, b=4, c=5"/>
<Label x={900} y={640} tone="accent">Legs 3 and 4 meet at 90 degrees.</Label>
<Arrow from="900,700" to="820,720" label="right angle"/>
</Canvas>
